hook: A program lives in people's heads.

beats.say: In nineteen eighty-five, Peter Naur argued that a program is mostly a theory held by the people who build it, not the code or the docs.
A program dies, he wrote, when the team holding its theory dissolves. It may keep running, but nobody can change it safely.
Coding agents fit the pattern: they can read every file, yet the understanding they build lasts only as long as the session.
